name: Bandelet Transform Analysis
description: Uses bandelet transform for edge-adapted geometric decomposition — captures geometric regularity deviations in AI images. Unlike wavelets that use fixed rectangular grids, bandelets adapt their basis functions along the geometric flow of edges, making them exceptionally sensitive to the unnaturally smooth edge geometry produced by AI generators.
algorithm: Bandelet Transform Coefficient Analysis with Geometric Flow Estimation
mechanism:
The bandelet transform (Le Pennec & Mallat, 2005) first estimates the local geometric flow direction of edges using a Lagrangian optimization, then decomposes the image along these flows using 1D wavelet transforms. This creates an edge-adapted multi-resolution representation where the coefficient decay rate reveals the geometric regularity of edges.

In natural photographs, edge geometry follows physically motivated contours with micro-irregularities from lens optics, sensor noise, and real-world surface roughness. AI generators, however, produce edges with unnaturally consistent geometric regularity — their Lipschitz exponents along detected flows cluster tightly around values typical of smooth manifolds rather than physical surfaces.

The detector computes: (1) the distribution of bandelet coefficient magnitudes at each decomposition scale, (2) the geometric flow consistency metric measuring how smoothly edge directions vary, and (3) the coefficient decay rate across scales compared to natural image statistics. An anomaly score is derived from the Kullback-Leibler divergence between observed and expected coefficient distributions.
parameters:
Decomposition levels: 3–5 scales
Geometric flow estimation: Lagrangian optimization with L² penalty
Wavelet basis: Alpert multiwavelets along flow
Coefficient analysis: per-scale kurtosis and decay rate
Statistical test: KL divergence against natural image model
accuracy: Moderate — 70-82% accuracy. Particularly effective for detecting diffusion-model outputs where edge geometry is systematically over-smoothed.
source: Le Pennec, E. & Mallat, S. (2005). Sparse Geometric Image Representations with Bandelets. IEEE TIP.
useCase: Forensic analysis of edge geometry regularity in suspected AI-generated images, detection of diffusion model outputs where geometric flow is unnaturally consistent, and complementary analysis alongside wavelet and contourlet forensic methods.
strengths:
• Captures geometric edge properties that standard wavelets and Fourier methods completely miss
• Highly sensitive to the over-smooth edge geometry characteristic of diffusion models (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E)
• The geometric flow estimation provides interpretable forensic evidence about edge irregularity
• Multi-scale analysis catches artifacts at different spatial resolutions
limitations:
• Computationally expensive — geometric flow estimation requires iterative optimization per image block
• Less effective on images with few edges (textures, flat backgrounds)
• JPEG compression disrupts the fine-scale bandelet coefficients most useful for detection
• GAN-generated images with adversarial edge sharpening can mimic natural Lipschitz regularity

references.title: Le Pennec, E. & Mallat, S. (2005). Sparse Geometric Image Representations with Bandelets. IEEE TIP.
Mallat, S. (2009). A Wavelet Tour of Signal Processing: The Sparse Way. Academic Press.
